title: Dense Chat burst allocator — headroom scenarios and regional targets
content:
Objective:
Produce quick reference peak projections and explicit headroom targets for the new 'Dense Chat' traffic pattern — multi-turn, high-token-density assistant sessions — and map required GPU pool sizing by region for Hosted API. This is a working-number sheet for SRE+Infra to review and convert into allocation plays and autoscale policies.

Executive summary:
- Dense Chat changes workload shape: average tokens/request ~3x baseline (longer responses), average requests/session higher (multi-turn), batching efficiency lower for short QPS bursts but higher for sustained sessions with KV cache reuse.
- We recommend a two-tiered headroom policy: 35% safety margin for on-net regions (primary capacity + rapid scaling), and 60% margin for newly launched regions or those with limited spare GPU inventory.
- Prewarm pool (cold-start buffer) should be set to 3% of steady-state capacity for standard gen models, and 6% for Dense Chat in top-3 regions.

Assumptions (base numbers used in calculations):
- Baseline (standard gen): avg tokens per request = 64 tokens; avg response latency target = 150ms; avg qps per request type = 1 request/sec per client in steady state.
- Dense Chat (multi-turn heavy): avg tokens per request = 190 tokens; mean session length = 5 requests; KV cache hit expected to reduce effective compute by ~25% for subsequent turns when cache warm.
- Model footprints: medium-large open model (22B) used as reference.
- GPU throughput estimates assume optimized runtime with batching and quantization profiles active.
- Target SLO: 99.9% p99 latency under peak headroom conditions.

Per-GPU throughput (approx, measured tokens/sec and QPS at avg seq length; include variability band):
- NVIDIA H100-80GB (fp16, tuned kernels):
  - Standard gen (64 tok): 12,500 tokens/sec per GPU (QPS ~195 at 64 tok/request)
  - Dense Chat (190 tok): 18,000 tokens/sec per GPU (QPS ~95 at 190 tok/request)
  - Notes: Dense Chat benefits from KV cache between turns; sustained sessions push throughput higher but increase memory pressure.

- NVIDIA A100-80GB (mixed):
  - Standard gen (64 tok): 8,600 tokens/sec per GPU (QPS ~134)
  - Dense Chat (190 tok): 11,900 tokens/sec per GPU (QPS ~62)

- NVIDIA L4 / L40 (inference-targeted):
  - Standard gen (64 tok): 4,400 tokens/sec per GPU (QPS ~69)
  - Dense Chat (190 tok): 6,200 tokens/sec per GPU (QPS ~32)

Throughput notes: tokens/sec scales roughly with sequence-length amortization and available FP throughput; QPS derived by tokens/sec divided by avg tokens/request. Numbers above include 1.15x effective throughput boost from continuous batching when average queue depth >2.

Regional projected peaks (example 99th-percentile 15-minute windows) — baseline vs Dense Chat surge scenario:
- us-east1 (N. Virginia):
  - Baseline peak (tokens/sec): 1,800,000
  - Dense Chat surge (tokens/sec): 3,900,000
  - Baseline QPS (at 64 tok): ~28,125
  - Dense Chat QPS (at 190 tok): ~20,526

- us-west1 (Oregon):
  - Baseline peak (tokens/sec): 820,000
  - Dense Chat surge (tokens/sec): 1,750,000

- europe-west1 (Belgium):
  - Baseline peak (tokens/sec): 620,000
  - Dense Chat surge (tokens/sec): 1,420,000

- asia-east1 (Taiwan):
  - Baseline peak (tokens/sec): 410,000
  - Dense Chat surge (tokens/sec): 970,000

Calculate needed GPU capacity (example for us-east1):
- Choose preferred SKU: H100 (primary). H100 tokens/sec for Dense Chat = 18,000.
- Raw GPUs required = ceil(3,900,000 / 18,000) = 217 GPUs.
- Apply safety margin: 35% => target pool size = ceil(217 * 1.35) = 293 GPUs.
- Prewarm pool (fast-start instances): 6% of steady-state for Dense Chat in top regions => prewarm = ceil(293 * 0.06) = 18 GPUs reserved for prewarm.

Capacity tables (condensed):
- us-east1 (Dense Chat): required H100 GPUs = 293 (target), prewarm = 18
- us-west1 (Dense Chat): raw = ceil(1,750,000 / 18,000) = 98 => target = ceil(98 * 1.35) = 133 GPUs, prewarm = 8
- europe-west1: raw = ceil(1,420,000 / 18,000) = 79 => target = 107 GPUs, prewarm = 6
- asia-east1: raw = ceil(970,000 / 18,000) = 54 => target = 73 GPUs, prewarm = 4

Fallback and routing policy recommendations:
- When H100 pool exhausted, automatically route to A100 pool in same region with dynamic model-variant flag (quantized variant) and throttle token-heavy calls signaled by header X-Client-Priority.
- Use region-to-region spill with priority: us-east1 -> us-west1 -> europe-west1 for NA-origin traffic. Maintain cross-region fallback budget: 12% of traffic allowed to spill under overload.

Autoscale triggers (operational heuristics):
- Soft scale-up: when 1-minute moving average utilization > 78% for 3 consecutive minutes, spin up warm nodes (prewarm) from reserved capacity.
- Hard scale-up: if p95 latency > 220ms OR queue depth > 1200 tokens for 2 minutes, add hot nodes from cloud inventory (or fallbacks).
- Scale-down: 10-minute sustained utilization < 42% and p99 latency < SLO => drain hot nodes (keep prewarm minimum).

Cost/back-of-envelope (approx):
- H100 hourly cost (reserved/committed pricing assumed) modeled at $2.95/hour (example internal blended rate).
- us-east1 Dense Chat steady cost: 293 * $2.95/hr = ~$864/hr => ~$620k/month (assuming 720hr).
- Note: use these numbers only for comparative planning; procurement should use exact committed SKU rates.

Operational runbook snippets (for playbook conversion):
- Pre-deployment: run synthetic Dense Chat workload (mean 190 tokens/request, 5-turn sessions) against new cluster to validate p99 latency <= 300ms at 75% target utilization.
- During surge: enable short-lived autoscale aggressor (reduce cooldown to 60s) and raise spill budget to 18% for 20 minutes if sustained overload.
- Post-surge: run sampling evals on model output for quality drift (higher quantization may reduce fidelity) and mark any model-variant degradations for rollback.

Open questions / data ops items:
- Validate actual observed tokens/request distribution for top 50 customers using Dense Chat; current 190 tok assumption needs confirmation.
- Measure KV cache warm-up curves across session index to refine per-GPU effective throughput for multi-turn sessions.
- Confirm committed H100 availability windows for prioritized regions for Q4 procurement planning.

Next steps (immediate):
- Owen / Priya to run a 3-region synthetic test (us-east1, us-west1, europe-west1) by 2026-07-27 and report empirical tokens/sec/GPU under live runtime.
- Diego to draft autoscale policy PR using the soft/hard triggers above for infra-ops review.
- Infra SRE to convert these targets into pool-sizing entries in the capacity-control spreadsheet (sheet id: CONVERT-LATER).

Appendix: quick formulas used (text):
- GPUs_required_raw = ceil(peak_tokens_sec / tokens_per_gpu_for_model)
- Target_pool = ceil(GPUs_required_raw * (1 + safety_margin))
- Prewarm_pool = ceil(Target_pool * prewarm_fraction)
